voices.note: Sukkah 2a.1: סוכה שהיא גבוהה למעלה מעשרים אמה פסולה ורבי יהודה מכשיר
Eruvin 2a, quoted תנן התם at Sukkah.2a.3: מבוי שהוא גבוה מעשרים אמה ימעט
subject of all three okimta chains (אמר רבי יאשיה אמר רב etc.); commits nothing directly -- the three versions are attribution-split, not self-contradiction
מכשיר in the mishnah; inside the 2b.14 baraita adduces the Helene maaseh and closes it at 3a.3
the sages: the mishnah's psul is theirs; the אמרו לו deflection inside the baraita (2b.15) and the צניעותא reading at 3a.3
the 2b.14 baraita: the mishnah's rule, R' Yehuda's forty-fifty bound, and the Helene-in-Lod maaseh

props.gloss_en: a sukkah higher than twenty amot is invalid
and R' Yehuda validates it (the 2b.14 baraita adds his bound: up to forty and fifty amot)
an alleyway-beam higher than twenty amot: he must lower it (R' Yehuda: he need not) -- the Eruvin mishnah whose תקנתא phrasing the מאי-שנא probe contrasts

Rabbah: the psul derives from 'that your generations may KNOW that I housed Israel in sukkot' -- above twenty the eye does not take in the sekhakh (דלא שלטא בה עינא) and the dweller does not know he sits in a sukkah
Rabbah's criterion: a sukkah requires the dweller's awareness of dwelling in it, and above twenty amot the eye no longer reaches the sekhakh
R' Zeira: the psul derives from 'and a sukkah shall be for shade by day from the heat'
R' Zeira's criterion: a sukkah requires that one sit in the shade OF THE SEKHAKH; above twenty amot one sits only in the shade of the walls
Rava: the psul derives from 'in sukkot shall you dwell seven days'
Rava's criterion: the Torah demands a TEMPORARY dwelling; above twenty amot one necessarily builds a fixed one
the others' ground against Rabbah's verse: למען ידעו speaks of the GENERATIONS' historical knowledge of the clouds of glory, not the sitter's awareness
the others' ground against R' Zeira's verse: וסוכה תהיה לצל is written of the messianic days
R' Zeira's counter: had the verse meant only the messianic canopy it would say חופה; from its saying סוכה, derive BOTH -- the canopy and the sukkah-as-shade law
R' Yoshiya's Rav: the machloket concerns a sukkah whose walls do not reach the sekhakh; walls reaching -- valid even above twenty
Rav Huna's Rav: the machloket concerns a sukkah of only four by four amot; larger -- valid even above twenty
Rav Chanan bar Rabbah's Rav: the machloket concerns a sukkah holding only his head, most of his body and his table; larger -- valid even above twenty

the joint content of Rav Huna's and Rav Chanan bar Rabbah's versions -- the machloket concerns a SMALL sukkah -- which the stam itself quantifies over at 3a.1 and which the Helene maaseh attacks. Gloss-only BY DESIGN: okimta/2 is declared functional below so that the three rival versions of Rav are visible to split_attribution/3, and this prop's content is entailed common ground of two of them, not a fourth rival value
the walls-reaching version runs like Rabbah: with walls reaching the sekhakh, the eye is led up to it and the dweller knows
the four-amot version runs like R' Zeira: in a spacious sukkah there is sekhakh-shade even above twenty

Rav Chanan bar Rabbah's version aligns with no one -- against Rabbah: head-and-table capacity neither helps nor hurts the eye's reach to the sekhakh (pairwise half of the דלא-כחד verdict; see header on the none-of quantifier gap)

and against R' Zeira: capacity of head-and-table is no measure of sekhakh-shade either; Rava is excluded already by his global psul above twenty, which admits no carve-out (glossed, not encoded -- header)
(entertained) Rav Huna and Rav Chanan bar Rabbah dispute the minimum valid sukkah itself
no: all agree the minimum valid sukkah holds head, most of the body and the table; they dispute the RANGE over which the tannaitic machloket runs (up to head-and-table vs up to four amot -- 2b.12-13)

the maaseh: Queen Helene's sukkah in Lod stood higher than twenty amot, and the elders went in and out and said nothing to her (R' Yehuda's proof that above twenty is valid). Content rides in the gloss: the maaseh's probative force is carried by the objection edges, and the Sukkah object-vocabulary is declared gloss-only debt (header)
R' Yehuda's second clause: everything Helene did, she did at the sages' direction
the sages' reading of the maaseh: her sons sat in the proper sukkah while she sat in the alcoves for modesty -- which is why the elders said nothing; the silence proves nothing

R' Yehuda's reading: her sons sat WITH her in the above-twenty alcove sukkah, and even so the elders said nothing -- the proof stands (gloss-only: its content would duplicate p_maaseh_helene's probative claim)

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה, העושה סוכתו בעשתרות קרנים — הכי נמי דלא הוי סוכה? if sekhakh-shade is the criterion, a sukkah in Ashterot Karnayim (shaded by the surrounding peaks, never by its own sekhakh) should be no sukkah

answered_by.gloss_en: התם, דל עשתרות קרנים — איכא צל סוכה; הכא, דל דפנות — ליכא צל סוכה: remove the mountains and sekhakh-shade remains; remove the above-twenty walls and no sekhakh-shade remains

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה, עשה מחיצות של ברזל וסיכך על גבן — הכי נמי דלא הוי סוכה? iron walls are the fixest of dwellings; on Rava's criterion such a sukkah should be invalid at any height

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמינא לך: עד עשרים אמה, דאדם עושה דירתו דירת עראי — כי עביד ליה דירת קבע נמי נפיק; למעלה מעשרים אמה, דאדם עושה דירתו דירת קבע — כי עביד ליה דירת עראי נמי לא נפיק: the criterion is the HEIGHT-CLASS, not the token building. Stands for Rava; the others treat Abaye's kushya as decisive (2b.4, commits)

objections.gloss_en: אמרו לו: משם ראייה? אשה היתה ופטורה מן הסוכה — a woman is exempt; her practice proves nothing

answered_by.gloss_en: והלא שבעה בנים הוו לה — of seven sons at least one no longer needed his mother and was obligated; ועוד, כל מעשיה לא עשתה אלא על פי חכמים (= p_al_pi_chachamim)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי (2b.14, carrying the baraita with R' Yehuda's forty-fifty bound and the maaseh): for the maaseh to engage the tannaitic machloket, per the small-sukkah versions Helene's above-twenty sukkah must have been SMALL -- and a queen does not sit in a small sukkah (3a.1)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא נצרכה אלא סוכה העשויה קיטוניות קיטוניות — a sukkah built as alcove upon alcove; itself challenged (וכי דרכה של מלכה לישב בסוכה העשויה קיטוניות קיטוניות?, 3a.2) and refined by Rav Ashi's okimta
לא נצרכה אלא לקיטוניות שבה — the proof concerns the small alcoves WITHIN her large sukkah; the closing machloket over what the elders' silence shows is p_rabanan_tznius vs p_yehuda_gabbah (3a.3)
